First, identify the away teams and their scores from the table:  

- St Kilda: 9.11 (65) → total points = 65  
- North Melbourne: 9.12 (66) → total points = 66  
- Richmond: 17.9 (111) → total points = 111  
- South Melbourne: 8.15 (63) → total points = 63  
- Geelong: 15.8 (98) → total points = 98  
- Melbourne: 8.10 (58) → total points = 58  

The statement says: "1 / 3 of the away teams had a score greater than 10."  
"Score" here means total points (the number in parentheses), not goals.  

Check each away team's total points > 10:  
All 6 away teams have scores greater than 10 (since the smallest is 58).  

So 6 out of 6 away teams satisfy "score > 10".  
1/3 of 6 = 2 teams.  
But here, 6 teams satisfy it, which is more than 2 teams.  

The statement says "1 / 3 of the away teams had a score greater than 10" — this means exactly 1/3 of them, not "at least 1/3".  
If 6 out of 6 satisfy it, that’s 100%, not 33.3%.  

So the statement is false.  

Final Answer: No
